newsitem.title: USA: Conoco to spend $1bn to develop Texas gas.
newsitem.headline: Conoco to spend $1bn to develop Texas gas.

text.p: Conoco Inc, a unit of Du Pont Co, said Friday it would spend $1 billion over the next five years to develop more than 2.7 trillion cubic feet (TCF) of proved and estimated natural gas reserves in the company's Lobo trend acreage in South Texas.

R.E. (Rob) McKee, Conoco's executive vice president of worldwide exploration and production, said the aggressive exploration and development program resulted from Conoco's acquisition of additional properties in the Lobo trend from First Intercontinental Leasing Trust.
The acquisition increases Conoco's U.S. natural gas production to approximately 1.0 billion cubic feet of gas per day (BCFD).
McKee said Conoco paid $900 million for the properties that were formerly owned by TransTexas Transmission Company.

He said the $1 billion investment would fund an aggressive exploration and development program with the goal of achieving a fivefold increase in Conoco's daily natural gas production from the Lobo trend.

"This acquisition is a key part of Conoco's long-term strategy to enhance its already strong position in the U.S. natural gas industry, and puts us farther along the road of doubling the value of Conoco by 2003," he said.

"Combining these new assets with our existing Lobo operations makes Conoco the largest producer in the Lobo trend; a leading producer, marketer and transporter of natural gas in South Texas; and the third largest natural gas producer in Texas," he added.
McKee said the future value of the newly acquired properties in the Lobo trend is as important to the company as the existing assets.

"Proved and estimated reserves in the new acreage are 1.8 TCF, and represent a 70-percent increase in our proved U.S. natural gas reserves," McKee emphasized. "Timely development of these reserves will strengthen Conoco's position in the natural gas business and will benefit the royalty owners and the State of Texas," he added.

McKee said the goal of the planned exploration and development program was to increase Conoco's net Lobo trend natural gas production from 165 million cubic feet per day (MMCFD) to 900 MMCFD within six years. He said the 1998 Lobo trend development program includes the acquisition of new 3-D seismic data and drilling 180 wells.

New Lobo trend assets acquired by Conoco include: 215,000 acres of leases, 1,100 wells, proven reserves totaling 250 billion cubic feet (BCF), and approximately 1,100 miles of natural gas gathering and transportation pipeline.
Conoco operates or has an interest in 24 natural gas processing plants in the U.S. and Trinidad with a net processing volume of 1.2 BCFD.
